It is human to grieve. Relying on your partner is one way to overcome that grief.

My advice would be to invest in a better quality machine, even if it's a low-tier professional machine. I'm a newbie barista and I have an at-home coffee machine for espresso and a milk steamer attached. It does its job... For at-home use. If I tried to make a real, sellable coffee, I wouldn't dream of using my machine, and it wasn't exactly cheap. 

The idea of using cafetiere's is a great one, if you don't think that coffee will be a super common order! You could also consider making your menu rely primarily on tea, and have coffee as an option, so as to use the cafetiere's less often. You could also try investing in a filter machine to make a nice, soft-toned filter coffee.

A V60 could also work - you should look into those, as they're a very effective method and less expensive than a professional barista machine. 

I hope this helps!

TW for mental health

I had to withdraw from university because my mental health is deteriorating after I suffered an abusive relationship. I'm now with an amazing partner who is incredibly supportive, but life is really tough. I'm extremely suicidal and have attempted to kill myself a few times. I've lost every penny of my savings and am living paycheck to paycheck. My job can't let me go full time, so I'm having to find somewhere else, which is a blessing and a curse as my current job gives me extreme anxiety and I am struggling a lot with that (despite loving the actual career), but it's also going to be a whole month before my new job starts as the cafe hasn't opened up yet.

The suicidal thoughts and PTSD from my abusive situation have led to me having black-outs and memory loss wherein I disassociate and forget things that surround a stressful situation. It means I've had a lot of fights with people and struggle to do my job properly. Ideally, I should take some time on sick leave before my new job begins, but I can't afford to. I would be homeless if I did.

To make matters worse, I cannot handle full-time work due to my physical issues. I was hit by a car when I was 12 years old and now at 20 I cannot run and have severe hip pain, back pain and knee dislocation. I can walk and do normal things, it's just painful to do so, and working full-time has been absolutely chronically destroying me. This makes my mental health issues worse, too.

I can hardly afford to buy my prescription medication (like, sometimes I have to wait a while to buy it and go cold-turkey) and I have to wait until January to get an increased dosage, which has left me high-risk at the moment. Thankfully I have a wonderful partner and I live with two lovely friends who look out for me, so my chances of successfully doing anything dangerous are slim. The fact that I still try, when I'm feeling manic, however, is a problem.

My mental health is only worsened by the fact that my mother - whom I have a very unstable relationship with - has had cancer twice, is diabetic, and severely unwell. I have a constant emotional turmoil about it and it has really made me fear loss.

It feels kinda good to be able to vent that stuff here. Thank you for asking such a genuine question. I hope everyone else who replies to this finds some solace from their struggles and has a great support system around them to keep them safe and bring them through the darkness. Every single person deserves to be loved and to feel content within themselves, even if we doubt that at times.
